transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?

I feel like certain people in my family and church are quietly working together against me, and no one believes me when I say it. My pastor recommended I come talk to someone to help keep the peace, but it is incredibly frustrating that everyone else thinks I'm just making this up.
Have you experienced any other unusual beliefs or perceptions that you're convinced are true, despite others telling you they're not, such as hearing voices or seeing things that others don't?

No, I definitely don't hear voices, see things, or experience anything strange like that. But I am absolutely certain that my sister-in-law and a few ladies from church are quietly spreading rumors that I can't be trusted with money. No matter how much my family tells me it's in my head, the things they do and say are just too coordinated to be a coincidence.
Have you taken any actions or made significant decisions based on your belief that these family members and church ladies are working against you?

I’ve started skipping some family get-togethers and church gatherings to avoid those women, which has caused a lot of tension with my husband and kids who say I'm overreacting and acting distant. But despite that, I still get to work on time every day, handle the billing, and take care of my mother and the house just like I always have.
Can you tell me more about how long you've been feeling like your family members and church ladies are working against you, and has this belief been persistent over time or has it come and gone?

This has been going on for about nine months now, starting right after a minor billing mistake I made at work. It hasn't come and gone at all; it's been constant and just keeps building because I'm always noticing little things, like missed invitations or side comments, that confirm what they are doing.
Have you ever had any periods where you doubted your belief about your family and church members working against you, or has your conviction in this belief remained unwavering since it started?

There are times I want to keep the peace, especially after a close friend tearfully suggested I see a doctor, which did make me doubt myself for a moment. But ultimately, all the little comments and coincidences keep adding up so perfectly that it's really hard to dismiss. It just feels too coordinated to be anything else.

You mentioned that your belief has been constant for about nine months, but with moments of doubt, such as when your friend suggested seeing a doctor. Can you tell me more about how often these moments of doubt occur and how long they typically last?

Those moments of doubt are actually very rare and only last for a brief moment before my conviction returns. I agreed to come here to keep the peace because my friend's reaction really made me pause, but all the small things like missed group texts and side comments are just too coordinated to ignore for long.

You've mentioned moments of doubt, but they seem brief. Can you estimate how much of the past nine months you've spent doubting your belief versus being completely convinced of the conspiracy against you?

I'm not really sure how to estimate the time, as I haven't ever thought about it that way. Most of the time I feel very convinced because everything fits together so perfectly, even though I sometimes wish it weren't true just to keep the peace.

Would you say that there has ever been a time, even if brief, when you completely lost belief in the conspiracy against you, or have you always, at some level, maintained the belief that something is being done against you?

No, I have never completely lost belief in it over these past nine months. Even though I get torn sometimes because I want to keep the peace and wish I was wrong, I have always maintained that they are working against me. All the coincidences, like being left off group texts and hearing those side comments, just fit together too perfectly to ignore.

Can you describe a specific situation where your belief in the conspiracy was significantly challenged, and how you responded to that challenge, to help me understand how your conviction in this belief has been maintained over time?

I confronted a longtime friend at the library about being part of this scheme, and she tearfully denied it and suggested I see a doctor. While that made me feel torn and I agreed to seek help to keep the peace, I still maintain my conviction. All the small details, like being left off group texts and hearing side comments, just fit together too perfectly to be a coincidence, despite what my husband and others claim.

Have you ever experienced any periods where you had a complete break from reality, such as hearing voices, seeing things that aren't there, or having any other experiences that seemed extremely real but weren't, even if it was just for a short time?

No, I have never heard voices, seen things, or had any kind of break from reality like that. But the situation with my sister-in-law and the ladies from church is completely real, not some illusion. Even though others keep telling me it's just in my head, these are actual things they are saying and doing.
